dedupe_keys.name: international grains council grain market report world and country supply and demand balances for grains rice and soyabeans free summary tables

description: These tables give the world balance sheet for wheat and coarse grains, rice and soyabeans: how much each major country produces, imports, eats, feeds to animals, exports and keeps in store, for the past, current and coming marketing year. The producer is the International Grains Council, the intergovernmental body behind the Grains Trade Convention, which publishes a monthly Grain Market Report. Coverage includes the main exporters and importers with world totals, and the September 2026 edition put world grain production at 2,420 million tonnes against 2,444 million tonnes of use and closing stocks of 608 million tonnes. Each workbook row gives opening stocks, production, imports, total supply, food, industrial and feed use, exports and closing stocks in million tonnes. The summary page and the three supply and demand workbooks are available as a free download, while the full report with detailed commentary and price data requires a paid subscription. Caveats: figures are forecasts revised every month, China is shown separately, and old editions must be kept by the user because links change each month. Simulation uses: setting stock buffers, import dependence and export shocks in global food supply disruption and trade models. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give longer historical balances.
